question: According to a 2023 Eurostat survey, Greece ranks first for unmet healthcare needs due to financial reasons (too expensive), waiting lists or distance from healthcare structures (too far to travel). Sadly, the need for bribes and connections undermines the quality of healthcare services offered to Greek citizens. In 2022, in the EU, 3.3 % of people in need of medical examinations were unable to undergo them.

The EU countries which reported the highest rates were: Greece (16.7 %), Finland (9.6 %), Romania (7.9 %) and Latvia (7.1 %). Obviously it is the more vulnerable social groups that suffer the most from being unable to meet their healthcare needs. In view of this: 1.

Can the Commission assess the effectiveness of the actions under the EU4Health programme in Greece, which aim to provide political guidance for mitigating the risk of poverty by minimising the impact of direct healthcare costs and looking at healthcare provision across all income groups?
What further initiatives is the Commission planning for the 2024-2029 period, in order to give all citizens access to essential medical examinations and to healthcare services?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (9.9.2024) The challenges Greece faces with access to healthcare are highlighted in various reports1,2. It is important to recall that the organisation and provision of health services is the competence of the Member States and EU action focuses on supporting the Member States.

Several EU4Health funded actions on access to healthcare include an action3 to assess the impact of healthcare coverage on poverty, an action4 to improve the affordability of healthcare, an action5 to improve access to healthcare for persons with disabilities and the European Cancer Inequalities Registry6. The mid-term evaluation of the EU4health programme is ongoing.

EU4Health annual work programmes, including possible future actions on access to healthcare, are developed on an annual basis taking into account priorities identified by the Member States and stakeholders. The Commission supports the resilience of Member States’ health systems through the Recovery and Resilience Facility7 complementing investments under Cohesion Policy funds under the 2021-27 programming period8.

Specifically, under the European Regional Development Fund, around EUR 367 million have been earmarked to co-finance infrastructure and equipment at all levels of care in the Greek National Health System under the 13 regional programmes.

In addition, EUR 240 million from the European Social Fund Plus (ESF+) has been earmarked by Greece to finance healthcare services in the 2021 – 2027 programming period, with an emphasis on community based primary healthcare. Furthermore, the Council Recommendation establishing a European Child Guarantee calls upon the Member States to guarantee, free and effective access to healthcare for all children in need.
Greece has prepared an action plan9.
